curriculumDefinition.commandsAndConcepts: `:normal`, `:normal!`; range and visual application; `:global`/`:g`; `:vglobal`/`:v`; global delete, substitute, normal commands, and macros; combined predicates and transformations
curriculumDefinition.learningOutcome: Apply Normal-mode edits across a controlled line set and choose the lowest-risk automation mechanism
curriculumDefinition.representativeExercises: Run a text-object edit on selected lines; delete debug lines; modify only declarations matching a predicate; execute a macro over matches
curriculumDefinition.priorityAndPortability: Core advanced automation. The distinction between mapped and unmapped Normal commands is explained, while mappings themselves stay out of scope

lessons.title: Run Normal commands over ranges
lessons.objective: Apply one Normal-mode command independently to every addressed line.

activities.title: Run one Normal command on every line in a range
activities.body: `:normal` starts at the first character of each addressed line and runs the supplied Normal-mode keys. Each line gets a separate execution.
activities.contrast: Use a range when the line set is already known; use a predicate when membership depends on text.

lessons.title: Choose the lowest-risk automation
lessons.objective: Select among ranges, predicates, substitutions, Normal commands, and macros.

activities.title: Choose the simplest automation for the task
activities.body: Use a range for known lines, substitution for direct text replacement, `:normal` for one structural edit, `:global` to choose lines by text, and a macro for a true multi-step edit.
activities.contrast: Advanced commands are valuable because they clarify intent, not because they are advanced.

activities.title: Choose the simplest safe mechanism
activities.prompt: The same short Normal-mode edit must run on lines 12 through 15, and those line numbers are already verified. What should you start with?

options.label: A `:global` command that replays a macro

activities.explanation: A known contiguous line set plus one local Normal command needs neither a predicate nor a macro.

activities.title: Scope first, transform second
activities.body: Use `:normal` for one Normal command across known lines, `:global` or `:vglobal` when text decides membership, substitution for clear textual replacement, and a macro only when the local edit is genuinely multi-step. Prefer the lowest-risk command that states the intent.
takeaways: Verify the range or predicate before Enter.
Test macros on representative rows before global replay.
Use `:normal!` when automation must ignore mappings.
